newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan gold, silver mine project in doldrums.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan gold, silver mine project in doldrums.

text.p: Pakistan's state-run Saindak Metals (Pvt) Ltd is in doldrums following a shortage of funds, officials of the mines project said on Tuesday.
The $373 million project, which started blister copper production in late 1995, was lying idle because of a shortage of funds, one official said.

The project's management asked Islamabad to give at least 1.3 billion rupees ($35 million) in the 1996/97 (July-June) budget to restart the blister copper production but could get only 10 percent, which was spent on salaries of more than 1,200 workers, the official said.
The management sold about 15,000 tonnes of blister copper worth 200 million rupees early this year but the money was also spent on salaries, the official said.

Developed by state-run Saindak Metals (Pvt) Ltd and aided by Chinese metallurgy experts, the mine began trial production in July last year. At certain stages, about 860 Chinese worked three shifts a day to complete the project.
Saindak was due to produce an estimated 1.47 tonnes of gold and 2.76 tonnes of silver a year as well as 15,810 tonnes of copper.
In 1987, China's Metallurgical Construction Corp (MCC) submitted a proposal to develop the mine on a turn-key basis.
Pakistan accepted the offer in 1988, after the Soviet Union began withdrawing its troops from neighbouring Afghanistan.
